title.narrative: Promoting community resilience through post-conflict recovery in the Gaza Strip

description.narrative:
The situation in Gaza presents an ongoing humanitarian emergency. The population of the overcrowded enclave has extremely high rates of poverty and unemployment, with a high incidence of injuries, chronic health problems and psychological distress. Its health service is vastly overstretched while at the same time burdened with shortages of medical supplies and fuel/ electricity. All these problems have been further intensified by periodic escalations of conflict - in particular that of May 2021 which caused major infrastructural damage - at a time when the Gaza health system has also been having to struggle with the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. The West Bank and Gaza has experienced a fourth wave of COVID-19 starting in January 2022 and peaking in February, and although reported cases declined rapidly after February this was noted to coincide with a drop in testing. As of June 2022 the number of cases in West Bank and Gaza stood at 660,000. In view of the underlying acute vulnerability of Gaza, the maintenance of satisfactory levels of health among the population generally should be seen as a high priority in supporting the process of recovery from the pandemic.
Crucial support will be delivered by Caritas Jerusalem through provision of a wide range of health services (primary healthcare, maternal and child health, management of communicable and non-communicable diseases along with health and nutrition education) to 7,400 patients. Approximately 450 of the patients presenting are expected to need referral for more advanced care: an estimated 200 will receive ENT, Eye and cardiology consultations from the Caritas team (due to their otherwise having to join very long waiting lists) and 250 treatment for Long COVID comprising symptomatic relief, breathing exercises and psychosocial support.
